components.input_conditions: One normalized sign direction and one radial cutoff as defined above.
components.parameter_and_cost_changes: Amplitude a h^beta; minimizer displacement (a/2)h^(beta-1); fixed T and h calibration above.
components.preserved_model_properties: Dimension-independent global strong convexity, gradient Lipschitzness and kth-derivative Holder bound.
remaining_obligations: For transfer, recheck the global derivative norm, aggregate signal inequality and information-to-error bridge.
components.transcript_control: Aggregate squared neighboring signals before any coordinatewise maximization.
components.transformation: Localize the whole linear perturbation with the same chi(||x||^2/h^2).

construction.definition: Set eta(t)=exp(-1/t) for t>0 and 0 otherwise, and chi(u)=eta(1-u)/(eta(1-u)+eta(u-1/4)). Then chi is C-infinity, valued in [0,1], equals 1 for u<=1/4 and 0 for u>=1. For unit v define F_v(w)=<v,w>chi(||w||^2). For s in {-1,+1}^d put v_s=s/sqrt(d), f_s(x)=||x||^2-a h^beta F_{v_s}(x/h).
construction.hidden_objects: The fixed sign vector s. Uniform averaging over the finite cube is a proof device; each hard instance is fixed before the algorithm's realized seed and observations.
construction.model_definition: For fixed finite real beta>2, k=ceil(beta)-1, alpha=beta-k in (0,1], p=(beta-1)/beta. F_beta(d) consists of f:R^d->R in C^k, with unique global minimizer x* in the closed Euclidean unit ball, and for every x,y in R^d: f(y)>=f(x)+<grad f(x),y-x>+||y-x||^2/2; ||grad f(x)-grad f(y)||<=3||x-y||; ||D^k f(x)-D^k f(y)||_op<=||x-y||^alpha. The operator norm is sup |A[u1,...,uk]| over independently chosen unit-ball directions.
construction.model_membership_argument: With q(w)=||w||^2, only Dq=2<w,u> and D^2q=2<u,u'> are nonzero. D^j(chi o q) sums over partitions into blocks of size 1 or 2. On ||w||<=1 each block contributes <=2 and each outer derivative is bounded, so K_j=sum_pi 2^(|pi|)||chi^(|pi|)||_infinity depends on j,chi only. Set K_0=1, M_0=1, M_j=K_j+jK_{j-1}; the linear-factor product rule bounds D^jF_v, and derivatives vanish outside the unit ball. The kth increment is <=min{2M_k,M_{k+1}||w-z||}, hence <=H_beta||w-z||^alpha by splitting distances at 1. The perturbation Hessian has norm <=a h^(beta-2)M_2<=1, so I<=Hess f_s<=3I globally. The quadratic kth derivative increment is zero for k>=2. Scaling the perturbation gives kth increment <=a H_beta h^(beta-k-alpha)||x-y||^alpha<=||x-y||^alpha. The proposed x_s*=(a/2)h^(beta-1)v_s has norm <=h/8< h/2, where chi=1 locally; grad f_s(x_s*)=2x_s*-a h^(beta-1)v_s=0. Global strong convexity gives the unique global minimizer, in B_2(1). For ||x||>=h all instances equal ||x||^2.
model_membership_refs: Same Source Lemmas 4.1-4.2 and A-B; membership proof below and batch Theorem formal model_membership link.
construction.parameters: Fixed beta>2 with k=ceil(beta)-1 and alpha=beta-k. Any positive integer d; 0<h<=1. For the fixed chi choose dimension-independent M_j bounding ||D^j F_v||_op and H_beta=max{2M_k,M_{k+1}}. Fix 0<a<=min{1/4,M_2^(-1),H_beta^(-1)}, omitting zero reciprocals. For budget T>=1 calibrate h=min{1,(d^2/(16a^2T))^(1/(2beta))}.
construction.public_information: d,beta,T,chi,a,h, entire family formula and standard Gaussian noise law may be public; only s is hidden.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Established by the explicit shared support.
escape_conditions.statement: Queries outside B_2(h) reveal no s-dependent information; unbounded query radius therefore does not escape this construction.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Argument limitation, not a proved faster algorithm.
escape_conditions.statement: Exact values, derivative feedback, common-noise pairs or changed noise laws are different experiments; this Gaussian KL argument alone supplies no lower bound there.

escape_conditions.epistemic_note: Transfer obligation; no universal impossibility claim for other constructions.
escape_conditions.statement: Separate coordinatewise cutoffs are not interchangeable with the common radial cutoff; the aggregate signal and derivative bounds must be proved anew.

hardness_claims.algorithm_coverage: Every measurable randomized fully adaptive algorithm with unrestricted query points and output, arbitrary computation and memory, and at most T calls on each run.
hardness_claims.missing_lifting: None for the stated normalized fresh-Gaussian-value model; altered noise, norm, oracle or function classes require new arguments.
hardness_claims.regime_note: All positive integers d,T; fixed finite beta>2; calibration includes constant-loss saturation.

oracle_realizations.choices_and_history: Instance s fixed before the run; algorithm private random seed independent of the hidden-instance averaging and noise. Conditional on a common history the action-selection kernel is identical under neighboring hypotheses.
oracle_realizations.cost: One independently corrupted scalar value per call; at most fixed T raw calls, with shorter runs padded by ignored zero queries.
oracle_realizations.information_bottleneck: For bit flip s^(i), delta_i(x)=-2a h^(beta-1)s_i x_i chi(||x||^2/h^2)/sqrt(d). Thus sum_i delta_i(x)^2=(4a^2h^(2beta-2)/d)||x||^2chi^2<=4a^2h^(2beta)/d globally. KL(P_s||P_s^(i))=(1/2)E_s sum_t delta_i(z_t)^2 for full seed/transcript/output. Kbar=(d 2^d)^(-1)sum_s sum_i KL<=2a^2T h^(2beta)/d^2. Far-away queries have exactly zero hidden signal.
oracle_realizations.information_to_error: Edge testing gives mean Hamming error >=(d/2)(1-sqrt(Kbar/2)). At the calibrated h, Kbar<=1/8, so mean Hamming error>=3d/8. Decode +1 for xhat_i>=0 and -1 otherwise; each wrong sign costs >=a^2h^(2beta-2)/(4d) squared distance to x_s*. Strong convexity gives mean expected gap >=3a^2h^(2beta-2)/64 >=(3a^2/64)min{1,(d^2/T)^p}, since 16a^2<=1. Consequently some fixed s is hard for each algorithm.
oracle_realizations.query_and_feedback: Any measurable adaptive query z_t in R^d receives Y_t=f_s(z_t)+xi_t.
oracle_realizations.sampling_and_reuse: xi_t iid N(0,1); fresh at every call, including repeated points. No exact values, gradients or shared noise across a pair.
supporting_claim_refs: Same Source C.1-C.2 and batch Theorem lower half.
oracle_realizations.testing_argument: For each undirected i-edge, the sum of the two error probabilities is >=1-TV(P_s,P_s^(i)). Averaging edges gives mean Hamming error >=d/2 times (1-directed-edge-average TV). Pinsker TV<=sqrt(KL/2) and Jensen bound the average TV by sqrt(Kbar/2). Gaussian KL follows by conditional chain rule: seed laws and action kernels agree, observation mean differences contribute delta_i^2/2, output uses a common conditional kernel. No extra information from adaptivity or unrestricted output is discarded.
